evals.prompt: The new invoice proration feature is green. Inspect the final diff and harden its tests before review.
evals.expected_output: Runs the green baseline, maps implementation-created edge cases, adds only behavioral tests or fixtures, and proves each addition without changing production code.
expectations: Requests or inspects acceptance criteria, final diff, plan edge cases, and existing tests
Runs the relevant suite before editing
Adds tests for observable behavior rather than private helper calls
Reports proof, omissions, and final suite result

evals.prompt: While hardening the completed parser, you discover that a valid empty document crashes production code.
evals.expected_output: Writes a failing public regression test and hands it back to the implementer. It does not repair production code in the hardening role.
expectations: Creates the smallest failing regression test
Requires hardening to be reconsidered after the implementation changes

evals.prompt: Start building a URL shortener with TDD. Write the first test and implementation.
evals.expected_output: Does not invoke test-hardening yet because this is initial TDD, not post-implementation hardening.
expectations: Uses ordinary red-green-refactor instead of post-implementation hardening
Does not claim a final-diff hardening pass exists before implementation is complete

evals.prompt: Increase coverage from 82% to 90% by adding any passing tests you can.
evals.expected_output: Rejects decorative coverage work unless each proposed test names a new observable contract or plausible fault it would catch.
expectations: Does not optimize blindly for a coverage number
Requires a concrete behavioral risk for every added test
